newsitem.title: JAPAN: APEC membership may be expanded this month.
newsitem.headline: APEC membership may be expanded this month.

text.p: Membership in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum could be expanded to countries such as Vietnam, as early as this month's summit meeting in Subic, a Philippine official and former trade minister said on Wednesday.
But only if ministers can agree on the criteria for admission, Rizalino Navarro, a special adviser to President Fidel Ramos on APEC affairs, told Reuters Financial Television in Tokyo.
"The timetable will depend on the criteria agreed on at the meeting for procedures of admission. But it then follows that anyone who qualifies will be admitted," said Navarro.
Asked if Vietnam could become a member at the Subic summit itself, he said: "It might happen."
"We have no doubt that Vietnam will become a member of APEC shortly," he said.

The moratorium on APEC membership expires this month and the issue of extension is to be discussed at the APEC ministerial meeting in Manila beginning November 22. The leader's summit will be held on November 25.
The Philippines, the current APEC chair holder, has indicated it does not want to see an extension.
"Rather than extend the moratorium, our more positive approach is to say we will open up the membership, but adopt some procedures, some criteria of admission," Navarro said.
Those criteria are thought to include suitable geographical location and a display of commitment to trade liberalisation.
Eleven countries have applied to become members of APEC, including Vietnam, Peru and Russia.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
